body.rationale: Governing IPS is still a draft, so I weighted the breaches as provisional. I am HRP and cannot rank myself. My own portfolio is a 92% cash corner with three hard breaches, so I looked for candidates the CIO can actually build from. First is pc_researcher: it has the best Sharpe among the compliant-ish candidates (0.51), a diffuse 7.2 effective N, a modest -10.9% backtest drawdown, and only two soft breaches (volatility and tracking error). Reviewers flagged that its narrative does not match what it delivered and that its Sharpe is above its stated floor. Those are fixable disclosure issues, not a flawed portfolio. Second is resampled_efficient_frontier: it has no hard IPS breaches, 13.3 effective N, and a covariance-based approach that is robust to noisy CMAs. Its main weakness is the thin drawdown headroom (-24.3% vs -25%) and the shared CMA bias, as the CVaR reviewer noted. Third is black_litterman: it has no breaches, 6.1 effective N, and a clean intra-category review that recomputed its numbers. The risks are sitting on the 8% volatility boundary and the -21.2% drawdown. Fourth is cvar_minimization: it has no breaches, the best drawdown of the three compliant return-optimised-style candidates (-18.7%), and a non-Gaussian tail focus that suits a late-cycle regime. It is fitted to a handful of crises, per the inverse_variance reviewer, and is concentrated at 2.9 effective N. Fifth is max_sharpe: it has no breaches and the best ex-ante Sharpe among the compliant set (0.46), but 46% in us_value rests on one judged CMA gap and its drawdown is -24.7%. First beats fifth because pc_researcher reaches similar or better Sharpe with much greater diversification and one third of the drawdown, and it does not rely on a single return forecast. For the flag I chose market_cap_weight: its -40.6% drawdown is far beyond the -25% limit, its CRO risk score is 0.80, and reviewers found the ETF-AUM proxy invalid because it double-counts overlapping asset classes and has no size measure for cash or gold. I did not flag the adversarial diversifier because its orthogonality has ensemble value.
